title: Voice Typing for RSI and Carpal Tunnel: A Practical Guide
summary: A guide to voice typing for RSI, carpal tunnel, and wrist pain: what the research says, how to set up hands-free dictation, and where it can't help.
body_markdown:
### Does voice typing cure or prevent carpal tunnel syndrome?


No. MedlinePlus (NIH) states researchers aren't even certain that long-term typing or computer use causes carpal tunnel syndrome in the first place, so there's no basis for claiming voice typing prevents or cures it. What it does is reduce the repetitive finger motion your hands do to produce the same amount of writing, one workplace accommodation among several, not medical treatment.\[2\]


### Is voice-to-text software actually a recognized accommodation for RSI or carpal tunnel?


Yes. The Job Accommodation Network, the U.S. Department of Labor-funded resource on workplace accommodations, lists voice-to-text and speech recognition software as a standard accommodation for cumulative trauma conditions such as carpal tunnel syndrome and tendinitis.\[1\]


### Do I have to hold a key down the whole time I'm dictating with VoiceOS?


Not necessarily. VoiceOS's default Dictation shortcut is hold-to-talk (hold it, speak, release), but VoiceOS also has a separate Hands-free shortcut that starts on one press and stops on a second press, so nothing needs to stay held down for the length of the dictation. Check Settings, General, Shortcuts to see or change which mode your Dictation trigger uses.


### Will voice typing let me stop using my keyboard and mouse completely?


No. Dictation Mode replaces typing specifically; it doesn't eliminate clicking, scrolling, or navigating with a mouse or trackpad. Pairing it with VoiceOS's Agent Mode for actions like opening apps or sending messages can reduce some of that, but Agent Mode can't type text into a field for you, that's still Dictation Mode's job.\[5\]


### Is there a time limit on a single VoiceOS dictation?


Yes. A single dictation currently warns at four and a half minutes and stops on its own at five, so a very long piece of writing needs to be dictated in more than one pass.


### What should I do if my hand pain doesn't improve after switching to voice typing?


See a doctor or occupational therapist. The NHS specifically recommends professional support, physiotherapy or occupational therapy, when RSI symptoms persist, and this guide isn't medical advice or a substitute for a diagnosis.\[3\]
